title: Kibble--Zurek Mechanism and Defect Freezing in Imbalanced-Pairing Kitaev Models
authors: R. Jafari, Alireza Akbari, Shukhrat Mardonov, A. Langari
abstract: We investigate driven dynamics across critical and exceptional points in the one- and two-dimensional imbalanced-pairing Kitaev models using both the wave-function normalization approach and the biorthogonal framework. For a positive pairing imbalance parameter, the quasiparticle spectrum remains real, and a pairing imbalance neither shifts the equilibrium phase boundaries nor generates imaginary eigenenergies. In this regime, the defect density follows the conventional Kibble--Zurek scaling in one dimension and the extended Kibble--Zurek scaling, arising from a gapless manifold, in two dimensions within both frameworks. The corresponding scaling exponents are therefore governed by those of the Hermitian transition. For a negative pairing imbalance parameter, time-reversal symmetry is broken, the quasiparticle spectrum develops complex eigenvalues, and the gap closes at exceptional points. For ramps ending at an exceptional point, the defect density follows the modified Kibble--Zurek scaling in the wave-function normalization approach, whereas it obeys the conventional Kibble--Zurek scaling in the biorthogonal framework. When the ramp traverses the time-reversal-symmetry-broken region, a finite density of defects remains even in the adiabatic limit, leading to defect freezing in both frameworks. Although this frozen background indicates a breakdown of adiabaticity, the excess defects generated on top of this background continue to obey the conventional Kibble--Zurek scaling in one dimension and the extended Kibble--Zurek scaling in two dimensions.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes defect production in imbalanced-pairing Kitaev models driven across quantum critical and exceptional points. By comparing two mathematical frameworks, the authors show how defect scaling laws are modified when time-reversal symmetry is broken, leading to phenomena like defect freezing. This provides critical insights into non-equilibrium physics in non-Hermitian quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics and defect production in imbalanced-pairing Kitaev models as the system is driven across critical and exceptional points.
main_result: The defect density exhibits conventional or extended Kibble-Zurek scaling in certain regimes, but traversing the time-reversal-symmetry-broken region leads to defect freezing, while excess defects still follow KZM scaling.
method: The analysis employs two distinct theoretical frameworks—the wave-function normalization approach and the biorthogonal framework—to study the time evolution governed by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is the one- and two-dimensional imbalanced-pairing Kitaev model, described by a time-dependent, non-Hermitian Hamiltonian $H(t)$ controlled by a parameter $h(t)$.
key_observables: Defect density ($n^d$), quasiparticle spectrum (real vs. complex eigenvalues), and the scaling exponents ($ eta$) of the defect production.
important_parameters: The pairing imbalance parameter (positive vs. negative), the nature of the quench (ending at a critical point vs. an exceptional point), and dimensionality (1D vs. 2D).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes initial preparation in the instantaneous right ground state, and defect freezing itself indicates a breakdown of adiabaticity.
paper_structure: The paper is structured by analyzing the dynamics using two frameworks (wave-function normalization and biorthogonal), detailing the model and phase diagram, deriving the quench dynamics, and finally investigating the specific defect production mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work extends critical dynamics concepts (KZM) into the non-Hermitian domain, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems, driven dynamics, and topological phases relevant to AMO physics.

FIG. 2. Scaling behavior of the excitation density as a function of the ramp time scale τ in the two-dimensional imbalanced-pairing Kitaev model for T -symmetric quenches with γ > 0. Panels (a) and (b) correspond to a ramp across a single critical point from µi = −4 to µf = 0.5, evaluated within the biorthogonal framework and the wave-function normalization approach, respectively. Panels (c) and (d) show the corresponding results for a ramp crossing two critical points from µi = −4 to µf = 4, within the biorthogonal framework and the wave- function normalization approach, respectively. The system size is Nx = 400 and Ny = 440.
